newsitem.title: USA: Mass. official urges pensions divest tobacco stock.
newsitem.headline: Mass. official urges pensions divest tobacco stock.

text.p: Massachusetts Treasurer Joseph Malone reiterated his determination to divest the state of its tobacco stocks, but told the Public Service Committee he needs legislative authority to do so, State House News Service reported.

Malone, who is expected to make a bid for the Republican slot in the 1998 gubernatorial race, said he wants to sell off the state's $190 million in tobacco holdings, which are part of the portfolio of stocks held by the state's $18 billion pension fund.
The Public Service legislative committee heard a bill on Tuesday authorizing Malone and and other fund managers to divest.
Current state law says the only factor managers can consider in their investment decisions is the financial interests of the workers who contribute to the pension fund.

Malone said last fall that the state had lobbied the tobacco companies in which it held stock to change their marketing practices, to no avail. So, Malone said, the time has come for the state to get rid of all its tobacco stocks.

"When the citizens of Massachusetts voted by referendum to spend almost $70 million each year to educate our youth about the dangers of smoking, the tobacco companies simply increased their advertising budgets...this insidious use of corporate resources to thwart these reforms and cultivate another generation of smokers should not be supported - however indirectly by public monies," Malone said.

A bill allowing divestiture passed the House last year and won initial approval in the Senate, but died with the end of the session. Rep. John Businger (D-Brookline) and other prime sponsors told the committee this could well be the year the bill makes it all the way through.
He said it was "unconscionable" that the state was invested in tobacco, "particularly now that the companies are about to admit their product causes illness and death."
